request.description: Deliberately unconstrained, and one field inside it is deliberately outside this contract: `recipient` (channel/config_id/external_user_id) travels in `send` requests whose audience is not the customer, and this schema asserts nothing about it (B1-5, T90/T214). The dispatcher refuses an unaddressable non-customer row before a request is ever built, so the guard is real but it lives in `OutboxDispatcher.dispatch_one`, not here. **A second send implementation must not read this silence as permission to ignore the field**: `RestrictedWeComProxyClient.send_text(guid=, recipient_id=, content=)` has zero production callers today and wiring it up is on M1b's path -- an adapter that honours only `conversation_id` puts a merchant's internal digest into that merchant's customer's chat, which is T90 verbatim. Whoever wires it either tightens this schema (a frozen-contract revision, named as such) or writes the triple-to-provider mapping down with a contract test. T214 holds the decision.
